The strongest evidence is the collapse in short-window equity correlation, active divergence against rising US risk assets, and only weak DXY linkage, although this is a contextual regime read rather than a directional guarantee.","analysis":"BTC currently screens as independent_pricing, meaning the short-cycle move is being driven more by crypto-specific catalysts than by the usual equity-and-dollar macro basket. In practical terms, BTC is not trading like a clean risk asset right now. That does not prove macro has stopped mattering or that this regime will persist; it only says the current aligned window shows much weaker co-movement with the normal cross-asset anchors than is typical.

The clearest evidence is in the equity correlations. BTC versus Nasdaq is 0.0699 on the 7-session window versus 0.3066 over 30 days, and BTC versus SPX is 0.0443 short-term versus 0.3501 over 30 days. Both relationships are weakening, which says BTC had some broader risk linkage over the month but has largely detached in the latest week. That matters because Nasdaq is the regime anchor here, and the short-window reading is far below the 0.30 invalidation threshold referenced in the watch conditions.

Outside equities, the picture is mixed rather than fully defensive. BTC versus Gold is 0.452 short-term versus 0.2291 over 30 days, so Gold linkage has strengthened, but the evidence explicitly says it is not strong enough to define a stable safe-haven regime. BTC versus Oil is -0.1932 short-term and -0.1569 over 30 days, a mildly negative and broadly stable relationship that looks more like short-cycle risk-appetite noise than a durable macro linkage. BTC versus DXY is -0.1199 short-term and -0.13 over 30 days, also stable and weak, which argues against a strong dollar-liquidity explanation dominating the tape right now.

Those correlations line up with the broader regime logic. Equity beta is weak, DXY liquidity is neutral, and Gold/Oil appetite is also neutral. The DXY context shows current at 27.715, 20-day average at 27.5742, 60-day average at 27.5821, and 20-day rate of change at 0.3803, with liquidity_regime classified as neutral. The Gold/Oil ratio is 34.0459 with a z-score of -0.5792, again leaving the broader risk-appetite read as neutral. So macro is not absent, but it is not delivering a strong unified message either. That lack of macro confirmation makes the crypto-specific explanation more credible.

Divergence is active, and that is the most important interpretive feature in the pack. The report says BTC fell while US risk assets rose and Nasdaq linkage weakened. The implication given is that BTC is carrying its own crypto-specific stress rather than simply tracking macro beta. In other words, if equities are firm while BTC underperforms and correlation to Nasdaq is falling at the same time, the read shifts away from "BTC as high-beta tech proxy" and toward "BTC is being repriced on its own catalyst set." This does not mean the divergence must continue, but while it remains active it argues against reading BTC through a simple risk-on/risk-off framework.

Pairwise aligned return rows are 42 for Nasdaq, SPX, Oil, and DXY, and 51 for Gold. Latest common dates are 2026-05-28 across all comparison assets. Fetch errors are null. The Nasdaq boundary distance is 0.2301, which leaves the regime read comfortably away from the 0.30 threshold rather than sitting on a fragile edge.

The main watchpoints are straightforward. First, monitor whether Nasdaq short-window correlation stays near 0.07 or climbs back through 0.30, because that would weaken the independent-pricing emphasis. Second, watch whether the BTC-versus-macro divergence persists for another aligned daily close; if opposing moves stop printing, the current interpretation loses force. Third, watch whether the DXY liquidity regime stays neutral or flips on fresh data, because a dollar-regime change could quickly alter the durability of the present read. The stated invalidation conditions are explicit: re-emphasize less independence if Nasdaq short-window correlation closes back at or above 0.30 from 0.07, recheck divergence if aligned BTC and macro returns stop moving against each other, and recheck the backdrop if the DXY liquidity regime moves away from neutral.

Bottom line: the current evidence says BTC is not trading as a straightforward macro risk asset. Monthly correlations still show some residual linkage to equities, but the latest week is dominated by detachment, active divergence, and a neutral dollar-and-risk-appetite backdrop.
